chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who became certain, after he had performed ẓuhr, that he had prayed five rakʿahs. He said: “And how did he become certain?” I said: He knew. He said: “If he knew that he had sat in the fourth, then the ẓuhr salat is complete; let him stand and add to the fifth rakʿah another rakʿah and two sajdahs, so that they become two rakʿahs of nafilah, and there is nothing upon him.”

key_terms.الظُّهْرَ: the ẓuhr salat, the noon prayer
key_terms.جَلَسَ: sat for the tashahhud in the fourth rakʿah
key_terms.خَمْسًا: five rakʿahs prayed instead of four
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيْنِ: the two prostrations completing a rakʿah

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if he becomes certain that he prayed five rakʿahs in ẓuhr salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who realizes with certainty after ẓuhr salat that he prayed five rakʿahs. If he had already sat in the fourth rakʿah, then his obligatory salat is valid, and he should add another rakʿah to make the extra into two rakʿahs of nafilah.
